label: Exposed postcolonial male Negritude's blind spots toward African patriarchy
description: Writing from Senghor's Senegal after the triumph of Francophone Negritude championed by Aimé Césaire and Senghor, Mariama Bâ showed in So Long a Letter how cultural decolonization preserved domestic patriarchy and caste prejudice.
dialecticalTension: Complements anti-colonial cultural affirmation with unflinching internal feminist critique.
historicalContext: Post-independence Francophone West African philosophy and literature (1979).

citations.author: Mariama Bâ
citations.work: So Long a Letter (Une si longue lettre)

label: Synthesized existential critique of immanence with Wolof ethical solidarity
description: Engaging French existential feminism in Dakar's intellectual milieu, Bâ reworked the critique of women's domestic confinement through Senegalese Islamic-modernist values and female friendship.
dialecticalTension: Rejects Western individualism while demanding African women's moral sovereignty.

citations.author: Obioma Nnaemeka
citations.work: Sisterhood, Feminisms and Power: From Africa to the Diaspora

label: Diagnosed postcolonial bourgeois mimicry and intimate alienation in West Africa
description: Mariama Bâ's literary-sociological dissection of the postcolonial African elite's moral compromises anticipated Achille Mbembe's later philosophical diagnosis of the "postcolony" and intimate power.
dialecticalTension: Reads state-level post-independence crisis through intimate domestic power relations.
